reasoning: Blunt trauma with hypotension (90/50), tachycardia (130), tachypnea (28), and hypoxia (SpO2 92%) indicate hemodynamic instability and shock physiology
Mechanism (fall from second story) plus abdominal pain and respiratory distress raise concern for internal hemorrhage (solid organ injury), hemo/pneumothorax, or tension physiology

Combination of shock index >1 and respiratory compromise suggests impending decompensation requiring immediate life-saving intervention (airway management, IV fluids/blood, possible surgical intervention)
Per ESI logic, unstable vitals with high-risk trauma mechanism meet criteria for ESI-1 rather than waiting to reassess as ESI-2
When torn between levels, err toward greater acuity given risk of rapid deterioration
